title: Curried Roasted Butternut Squash Soup with Coconut and Coriander
changes_from_base: Same roasted squash soup with curry powder and ginger cooked into the base, coconut milk instead of cream, and coriander instead of sage and pumpkin seeds.
summary: This follows the classic roasted butternut squash soup method, with curry powder and ginger cooked into the base, coconut milk instead of cream, and fresh coriander in place of sage and pumpkin seeds.

ingredients.item: butternut squash (1 large), peeled, seeded and cut into 3 cm chunks (about 1 kg prepared)
fine sea salt or table salt
coconut milk, plus 2 tbsp to swirl

steps.title: Roast the squash
steps.text: Here the classic roasted squash method gets a curry and coconut twist. Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C), toss the squash with the oil and a pinch of the salt on the lined tin and roast for 35-40 min, turning once, until soft and browned at the edges. Browning adds sweetness that stands up well to the spices.

steps.title: Bloom the spices
steps.text: While the squash roasts, melt the butter in the pot over medium heat and soften the onion and carrot in it for 8 min. Add the garlic, curry powder and ginger and stir for 1 min until fragrant. Frying the spices briefly in fat releases their aromatic oils and removes any raw, dusty taste.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the roasted squash, broth, water, remaining salt and pepper, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 min. The vegetables should be completely tender and easy to crush against the pot.

steps.title: Blend and enrich
steps.text: Blend until very smooth, filling an upright blender no more than half full and holding the lid down with a towel. Stir in the 200 ml coconut milk and lemon juice and reheat until steaming and just bubbling, thinning with water if needed. Gentle heat keeps the coconut milk from splitting.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Ladle into bowls, swirl in the remaining coconut milk and top with coriander and a pinch of chilli flakes if you like some heat.

tips: A common mistake is adding curry powder straight to the liquid, where it tastes raw; always fry it with the onions first.
Shake the coconut milk tin well before measuring, as the cream separates on standing.
Keep the chilli flakes on the side if serving children or anyone sensitive to heat.
Avoid boiling hard after adding the coconut milk to keep the soup smooth.
storage: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat until boiling hot (74°C), stirring often.
